model_output.verdict: Strong program results at Google and Dell sit behind a current operations role that leaves too much to guess.
write_up: You’ve moved from supply chain work at Dell to data center planning at Google and now manage a freight terminal at Brightline. It’s common to summarize a current job as a list of duties, but those duties don’t distinguish your terminal work in a pile. I read this for Operations Manager roles.

Your Google line about cutting the forecast-to-delivery cycle is the model: it names the change and the approvals you consolidated to make it happen. The current role doesn’t give a recruiter the same footing, especially on how much terminal activity or how many people you manage.

Let’s start with the daily operations line, then add the team’s size and the work behind the carrier and customer issues. Bring the same detail you used at Google to Brightline, using only figures and results you can stand behind.

cards.line: - Responsible for daily operations of the Austin terminal
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can’t tell what daily operations cover or how much activity the terminal handles. Those details help establish the remit of your current role.
cards.example: Responsible for daily operations of the Austin terminal, including [work handled] and [measure of terminal activity]
cards.question: What do daily operations include, and how much activity does the terminal handle?

cards.line: - Manage a team of coordinators and dispatchers
cards.cannot_tell: The team’s work and size are missing. A recruiter looking at a manager role will want to know both.
cards.example: Manage a team of [number] coordinators and dispatchers who [work handled]
cards.question: How many people do you manage, and what does the team handle?

cards.line: - Work with carriers and customers to resolve issues
cards.cannot_tell: It’s not clear which issues come to you or what your part in resolving them looks like. One real example would give the work a shape.
cards.example: Work with carriers and customers to resolve [type of issue] by [your part in resolving it]
cards.question: What kind of issue have you resolved with carriers and customers, and what did you do?

cards.line: - Report weekly metrics to the regional director
cards.cannot_tell: The metrics aren’t named, so a recruiter can’t tell what you track or how the reports are used.
cards.example: Report weekly [metrics] to the regional director to support [decision]
cards.question: Which metrics do you report, and what decisions do they support?

cards.line: - Cut the forecast-to-delivery cycle for new capacity from 14 months to 9 by consolidating three approval tracks into one
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It gives a recruiter the before and after, then names the change you made to the approval process.

fit.why: Your current role manages the Austin terminal and a team of coordinators and dispatchers.
fit.level: Manager, with a current team and prior management of 6 program managers
fit.note: Your current work points toward terminal operations management, while Google and Dell show substantial program management work. Add the size and substance of the current role so a recruiter can compare it with the earlier work.
